blocks.content: ARG defines a variable that is only available during the build, and disappears entirely once the image is finished, it never exists inside a running container.

ARG exists purely to parameterize the build itself, things like a version number to install or a flag that changes which build steps run, values that matter while building, but have no reason to persist afterward.

blocks.alt: Scoped strictly to the build process itself

blocks.content: This is the sharpest distinction from ENV: an ARG value is not baked into the final image at all, if your running application tries to read it as an environment variable, it simply will not be there.

blocks.alt: Not present in the container once it is running

blocks.content: 3. Overriding an ARG at Build Time
blocks.text: 3. Overriding an ARG at Build Time

blocks.content: The default value an ARG declares in the Dockerfile can be overridden right on the docker build command, without editing the Dockerfile itself, exactly the mechanism CI pipelines use to inject a build-specific version number or git commit hash.

blocks.alt: A build-time override, no Dockerfile edit needed

blocks.title: Key Takeaway
points: ARG values exist only during the build and are gone entirely once the image is finished, never visible inside a running container.
Use ARG for build-time parameters (a version, a flag), use ENV for anything the running application actually needs to read.
